nodes.question: According to Verplanken and Wood (2006), what is one benefit of smart energy technologies, including energy apps?
nodes.answer: Smart energy technologies can encourage reflective energy use by providing actionable feedback to users.
nodes.paragraph: Further, Wemyss et al. (2023) emphasise the importance of moving beyond the initial excite- ment around these technologies to understand better the conditions under which they function as social innovations contributing to low-carbon transitions. This perspective underscores the need to study energy apps as mediators of user engage- ment, providing insight into how digital interfaces influence interactions with energy data and inform decision-making. The COVID-19 pandemic has further amplified interest in digital solutions that support sustain- able lifestyles as environmental awareness became a more salient priority for consumers (World Eco- nomic Forum, 2020). Lockdowns and remote work increased reliance on digital tools for managing daily activities, including energy consumption (Gunaratna & Aslam, 2022). This shift created opportunities for digital energy solutions, such as smart energy apps, to play a greater role in household energy manage- ment. Verplanken and Wood (2006) highlight that smart energy technologies, including energy apps, can encourage reflective energy use by providing actionable feedback. Similarly, Sanguinetti et al. (2018) emphasise that user interaction with these technologies can enhance awareness of energy-effi- cient practices.
